sources.citation: Grimes, Charles E. & Owen Edwards. 2026. The Austronesian languages of eastern Indonesia and Timor-Leste: Unravelling their prehistory and classification (Languages of the New Guinea Region). Berlin: Language Science Press. DOI 10.5281/zenodo.18323007. Sec. 4.7 'Southwest Tanimbar', pp. 240-248; also p. 444.
sources.note: Historical phonology only. Sec. 4.7 gives Makatian/Seluwasan/Selaru sound correspondences (*p > zero, *l > dʒ/d, *R reflexes) from Conner 2012 wordlists and Edwards fieldnotes; nothing on Seluwasan stress (a full-text search for stress/accent the LaTeX sources and full PDF text: no 'stress'/'accent' in the Southwest Tanimbar section). p. 444 states stress for relatives only: 'In Fordata, stress is penultimate. In Yamdena stress is normally penultimate, but can shift to the ultimate syllable with the addition of plural -ar. In Kei stress is ultimate.'

sources.citation: Soemarsono, Dian Wahyu P. & Deby Marlina Kewilaa. 2025. Transfer of learning Selwasa Language in informal education in Marantutul Village, Tanimbar Islands Regency. Journal of Social, Humanity, and Education 5(3): 225-238. doi:10.35912/jshe.v5i3.2498.
sources.note: No phonology content: qualitative education study of how parents transmit Selwasa (direct pronunciation practice, vocabulary teaching, storytelling, games). Mentions a YPMD-led programme producing reading materials and scripture in the five Tanimbar languages (after Luturmas et al. 2022) but cites no linguistic description.
sources.venue: Journal of Social, Humanity, and Education

sources.citation: Paembonan, Herni. 2024. Mengenal Bahasa Daerah di Kepulauan Tanimbar [Getting to know the regional languages of the Tanimbar Islands]. Web article (rubrik Artikel), Balai Bahasa Provinsi Maluku, Badan Pengembangan dan Pembinaan Bahasa, Ambon; posted June 2024 (author: 'Herni Paembonan, S.S., Widyabasa Ahli Pertama Kantor Bahasa Provinsi Maluku'). Reprinted by siwalima.id.
sources.note: Nothing. Popular summary of the Peta Bahasa entries (accessed 29 May 2024): method (Guiter dialectometry thresholds, the 200+52+25+98+25+822-item Badan Bahasa questionnaire), then per language: locations, vitality and dialectometric difference percentages (Makatian vs Seluwarsa/Yamdena 95%; Seluwarsa vs Selaru/Yamdena 81-100%; Seluwarsa obligatory in adat ceremonies). No forms, no phonology; 'tekanan', 'aksen', 'nada', 'fonologi' do not occur ('intonasi' once, in the generic definition of 'wicara').

sources.citation: Schapper, Antoinette & Erik Zobel. 2024. Languages of Timor and southern Maluku. Chapter 35 in Alexander Adelaar & Antoinette Schapper (eds.), The Oxford Guide to the Malayo-Polynesian Languages of Southeast Asia, 567-595. Oxford: Oxford University Press. DOI 10.1093/oso/9780198807353.003.0035.
sources.note: Nothing on stress/tone; named only as a language omitted from the survey: 'for Seluwasan on Tanimbar not even a wordlist has been published' (p595). The chapter's stress section (35.2.4, p570) names Roma, Leti, Fordata, Selaru, Dobel, Kola, Batuley only.
sources.venue: The Oxford Guide to the Malayo-Polynesian Languages of Southeast Asia

sources.citation: Fenanlabir, Ursula Margarita, Romilda Arivina Da Costa & Leonora F. Pesiwarissa. 2023. Pemertahanan bahasa Selwasa di Desa Batu Putih, Kecamatan Wermaktian, Kabupaten Kepulauan Tanimbar. ARBITRER: Jurnal Pendidikan Bahasa dan Sastra Indonesia (Universitas Pattimura) 5(3): 973-988. doi:10.30598/arbitrervol5no3hlm973-988.
sources.note: No phonology content: a language-maintenance study (domains of use by generation and occupation, Selwasa vs Ambon Malay percentages, interview excerpts). No word-level transcription, no mention of tekanan/aksen/nada. Reference list contains no structural description of Selwasa.

sources.citation: Erniati. 2018. Mengenal bahasa Makatian di Kepulauan Tanimbar [Getting to know the Makatian language in the Tanimbar Islands]. Web article (rubrik Artikel), Kantor Bahasa Maluku, Badan Pengembangan dan Pembinaan Bahasa, Ambon; posted November 2018 (author: 'Erniati, S.S., Peneliti pada Kantor Bahasa Maluku').
sources.note: No phonology content. A popular report: Badan Bahasa's mapping had identified four Tanimbar languages (Yamdena, Fordata, Selaru, 'Seluarsa'); locals reported a further isolect, Makatian; the Kantor Bahasa Maluku Tim Pemetaan Bahasa travelled to Desa Makatian to inventory its vocabulary for dialectometric analysis; notes on vitality (children still speak it), informant selection, mixed marriages with Seluarsa/Yamdena/Fordata/Selaru speakers, and a village 'Tim Bahasa Makatian'. No word 'tekanan', 'aksen', 'nada', 'fonologi' or 'bunyi' occurs in the text; no forms are cited.

sources.citation: Hughes, Jock. 1987. The languages of Kei, Tanimbar and Aru: Lexicostatistic classification. In Soenjono Dardjowidjojo (ed.), Miscellaneous studies of Indonesian and other languages in Indonesia, part 9 (NUSA 27), 71-111. Jakarta: Universitas Katolik Indonesia Atma Jaya. Sec. 2.1.2.6 'Seluwasan', p. 89.
sources.note: Silent. The Seluwasan section (p. 89) gives location (Wermatang, Batu Putih, Marantutul + divergent Makatian dialect, c. 2,100 speakers), lexical similarity (Wermatang-Makatian 86%) and intelligibility anecdotes; no phonology. scanned of all 41 pages finds no 'stress'/'accent' anywhere; stress marks appear only in a table of Yamdena dialect forms (p. 104). Seluwasan wordlists themselves are not printed.
sources.venue: Miscellaneous studies of Indonesian and other languages in Indonesia, part 9 (NUSA 27)
